legend: Krampus (Alpine winter folklore, Austria and Bavaria)
lines: High in the Alps, the night of December fifth was once a night to fear.
Tradition says Saint Nicholas never walks alone.
At his side stalks Krampus, a horned beast with the legs of a goat.
He drags rusty chains and carries a bundle of birch twigs.
Legend says he came for children who had been naughty all year.
Villagers listened for the clang of his chains in the snow.
Doors were barred, and the candles burned low.
Even today, men in shaggy masks run through Austrian streets that night.
If you heard chains in the snow tonight, would you open the door?
title: The Alpine Beast Who Hunts Naughty Children #shorts
description:
In Alpine folklore, Krampus is a horned, goat-legged beast who walks beside Saint Nicholas on the night of December fifth, dragging chains.
